tr.td: Dermoscopy of the right great toenail by the clinic's dermatologist: a brown-black background band about 5 mm wide with longitudinal lines irregular in color, thickness and spacing, and pigment on the proximal nail fold and hyponychium (micro-Hutchinson sign); suspicious for melanoma

Full-thickness excisional biopsy of the nail matrix at the origin of the band, after reflecting the proximal nail fold, under a digital block: acral lentiginous melanoma, Breslow thickness 0.8 mm, not ulcerated, mitotic rate 1 per mm2, no lymphovascular or perineural invasion, melanoma in situ extending to the lateral edges of the specimen
Advance care planning conversation, about 16 minutes
Preoperative lymphoscintigraphy with SPECT/CT after injection around the right great toe: drainage to two right superficial inguinal sentinel nodes; no popliteal drainage

Digit-sparing en bloc excision of the whole nail unit of the right great toe (nail plate, matrix, bed, hyponychium and nail folds) down to the bone, including the periosteum of the distal phalanx, with 5 to 10 mm margins. Pathology: residual melanoma in situ over 3 mm at the biopsy site and no residual invasive melanoma; all margins clear, the closest 6 mm
Full-thickness skin graft from the inner right upper arm to the defect on the right great toe, with a tie-over dressing

Right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy: two sentinel nodes removed, both negative for melanoma on serial sections and immunohistochemistry (SOX10 and Melan-A). Final stage pT1b pN0(sn) M0, AJCC 8th edition pathologic stage IA

Biopsy result: acral melanoma of the toe; surgical oncology consultation, staging, and a shared decision about surgery
Review two weeks after digit-sparing excision and sentinel node biopsy: final pathology and stage, graft care, and the surveillance plan
Three-month melanoma review: graft, nodes, full skin and nail examination, and self-examination
Same-day sick visit for a twisted ankle at football

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Surgical oncology consultation for a suspected subungual melanoma, to plan staging and definitive surgery once the biopsy result is back

Dermoscopy of the nail and a full-thickness biopsy of the nail matrix at the origin of the band by the clinic's dermatologist within the week, with a full skin and nail examination including the palms and soles

Staging by the AJCC 8th edition: examination of the lymph node basins, no routine imaging or blood tests for clinical stage I disease, and sentinel lymph node biopsy of the right groin discussed and offered for a T1b melanoma

A shared decision on definitive surgery: amputation of the toe at the interphalangeal joint, or digit-sparing en bloc excision of the whole nail unit down to the bone with a 5 to 10 mm margin and a full-thickness skin graft, an accepted option for a thin melanoma of the nail unit; he chose the digit-sparing excision, with amputation as the agreed next step if the margins were involved or the melanoma proved thicker

No adjuvant systemic therapy for pathologic stage IA melanoma; surveillance with a history and examination of the skin, nails, graft and lymph nodes every 6 to 12 months for 5 years and then yearly, a yearly full skin examination by dermatology, and no routine imaging or blood tests

Skin self-examination every month, with a mirror and in good light: the palms, the soles, between the toes and all the fingernails and toenails, the sites people with darker skin most need to check, as well as the graft and both groins; photographs of the graft; report any new dark band, spot, lump or sore that does not heal
Graft and wound care, a stiff-soled protective shoe, and a graded return to running and football once the graft has healed
Tissue diagnosis within two weeks of presentation
Dermoscopy and nail matrix biopsy two days after presentation; diagnosis explained on the ninth day
Definitive surgery with clear margins and lymph node staging within four weeks of diagnosis, by the approach he chose
Digit-sparing excision of the nail unit with clear margins and a negative sentinel node two weeks after diagnosis
Walk, run, and play football normally within four months of surgery
Running and playing football again; an ankle sprain at football healed in four weeks
Monthly skin and nail self-examination, including the palms, soles, between the toes and all nails
Taught after surgery; he has done it each month and keeps photographs of the graft
